THE PLANNER MEASURABLE — how we know Richie is actually planning
The failure mode is not laziness. It is REACTING TO THE DAY instead of BUILDING THE WEEK. So the measure has to catch proactivity, not effort.
Two numbers. One machine-checked, one reported by the person who gets hurt when it is missed. Neither is self-reported by Richie.

column2: NUMBER 1 — MONDAY OVERLOAD COUNT

column1: What
column2: Days in the coming week where any production lane is scheduled above 100% of its 8-hour capacity. Measured Monday 8:00am.

column1: Why
column2: A planned week is a week that FITS. An unplanned week is a pile of due dates that happen to be in the same calendar.
This is the one thing only the Planner can do, and the one thing no automation can do for him.

column1: Target
column2: 0 red days.  1 is yellow. 2 or more means the week was not planned, it was accepted.

column1: How
column2: The block sweep already computes it and prints it as DAILY LOAD. No new tool. Nobody types anything.

column1: Baseline
column2: Sept 29: THREE red days in six — Tue EMB 384%, Wed Screen Print 217%, Fri EMB 144%. That is the number we are starting from.

column1: Owner
column2: Richie owns it. Resolving it means moving jobs, adding a shift, or calling the customer. All three are Planner decisions.
WHY NOT "DOES EVERY JOB HAVE A BLOCK?"
Because the sweep places the blocks itself, every two hours. That number would read 100% forever and measure the robot, not the man.
The robot can place a block. It cannot decide that Wednesday will not fit and something has to move. That is the seat.
NUMBER 2 — NEXT-DAY SCREENS READY

column1: What
column2: Days out of 5 that screens for the next day's schedule were burned and racked before Richie left.

column1: Why
column2: This is the handoff from the week to the day. If it is missed, the Executioner starts the morning behind.

column1: Target
column2: 5 of 5.  4 of 5 is yellow. 3 or below is red and goes straight to the Issues List.

column1: How
column2: Justin calls it at the morning meeting in one word. Ten seconds. The consumer of the work reports it, never the producer.

column1: Owner
column2: Richie owns the number. Justin reports it. That separation is the whole point.
